payload.ranking:
U1 THE WHOLE TRANSPORT - already settled, promoted in rather than spiked. Encrypt, publish, serve as HTML, read-after-write, and a three-action card with a view link were all exercised live before the requirements gate (run-bfd564ff9add). What if wrong: the iteration is impossible. Remaining doubt: none server-side.

U2 THE TAP AND THE RENDER - the one that matters, and the one no spike can close. Does the card render as a gate on the actual device, does the view action open the page, does the page decrypt in that browser, and does the tap return a grant? WHAT IF WRONG: exactly the failure this iteration exists to fix, shipped again. Damage: total. Doubt: MODERATE - the transport is proven and v1's shape is proven, but the browser-side decryption in the page is genuinely new and untested on that device. NOT SPIKEABLE by the agent: it needs the owner's thumb, so it IS the demonstration D1 and it is bound to this iteration's own release gate.

U3 BROWSER-SIDE DECRYPTION - the half of U2 that CAN be tested without a phone. Does the inline decryptor actually recover the plaintext from the published ciphertext, using the key from the fragment, under the Web Crypto API? WHAT IF WRONG: the owner opens a page that says 'could not decrypt' and the brief is worthless even though every server-side check passed. Damage: high. Doubt: high - the probe verified only that ciphertext was stored, never that it round-trips.

U4 SILENCE WHEN SELF-BLESSING - can the announce path actually know that the run will self-bless, at the moment it decides? WHAT IF WRONG: either the owner is buzzed through unattended runs, or the corrected rule cannot be implemented as stated. Damage: moderate. Doubt: low-moderate - the caller knows, but the plumbing has to carry it.

U5 CONFIG READ AT ANNOUNCE TIME - trivial mechanically, but it changes where the lane's state lives. Damage: low. Doubt: low. Not spiked; it is build work.
payload.seeded:
Two spikes, both tight, plus the demonstration that is not a spike.

SPIKE SP1 - THE DECRYPTION ROUND TRIP (covers U3). Timebox: 20 minutes. Question: does a page produced by the brief renderer decrypt its own ciphertext with the key taken from the fragment? Success: the plaintext marker is recovered by the same Web Crypto path a browser would use, from the exact bytes that were published. Failure: any mismatch in the encoding, the IV or the auth-tag layout - the three places this quietly goes wrong. This is the highest-value spike because it is the only way the brief can be broken while every other check is green.

SPIKE SP2 - THE WAIT SIGNAL (covers U4). Timebox: 15 minutes. Question: at the moment a gate is offered, can the announce path tell whether this run will park for a human or bless it itself? Success: a single explicit signal carried from the caller, with no inference from configuration. Failure: the information is not available where the decision is made, in which case the design must move the decision rather than guess.

NOT A SPIKE, and named so it is not mistaken for one: U2's render-and-tap is the owner's release-gate bless. Its authority is a real device, and no amount of agent-side probing substitutes for it - which is precisely the lesson of the iteration this one repairs.
